doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

title: Chris Kelly's funeral and death
summary: Edna describes the huge funeral with seven bands and says Chris died at Lincoln Bell, which she links to drinking.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Oh, everybody. White and colored. Everybody. White and colored. Everybody. He had a funeral. It was long, it was from where I'm sitting, almost to Espinay Street. Yes. But the rain came out and there was, the people was willing to walk with the bands. He had seven bands volunteered behind. Where did the funeral start? Where it started at? It started from Sinan and Derry. I had them laid out by his sister, by his niece's house. My name was Lena Polder. And the funeral started from there, from the house. You know, they used to lay people out in the house at the time. And people gathered all around the house and the bands were coming. And the limousines, you know, picked us up. We all got in there. And a line of people I never saw the end of. So Lorraine come down and they told me about it. You know, for a while. How long was I? See, we was in the limousines. They was walking. Oh, did they have one. White and black. Everybody. Looked like everybody turned out this day.
And this is two, if you know, and love.
And then we have time and so it's been. There's two days I know.
Yes. How about it? Yes, how about it? You're planning on it? Yes. Interesting. Yes. Can you, do you know what Chris died of? Why he died?
He died at Lincoln Bell of the Heart.
Oh, really? Yes. He had a bad heart on the wrist.
No. He was, you know, by drinking, he used to like to drink.
